name: NY-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Tim Kennedy running with a large fundraising edge ($2.3M raised)
Prediction markets price Kennedy at ~94% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Kennedy: a D+11 district, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising advantage over Dennis Hannon, with markets pricing a Democratic win near certainty. No polls or expert ratings contradict this picture, so the forecast stays at a Safe D margin of about 21 points.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for Hannon or an unexpectedly favorable national environment for Republicans could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
NY-26 is a Buffalo-area district that leans Democratic by about 11 points, and incumbent Tim Kennedy is seeking reelection after winning the seat in a special election. Kennedy has raised roughly $2.3 million and holds over $1.2 million on hand, while Republican Dennis Hannon reports no significant fundraising in the available data.

No general-election polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money, all of which favor Kennedy. Prediction markets also price a Democratic win at roughly 94 percent. The race is rated Safe D, with Kennedy favored by around 21 points.
